candidates.attacker_control: Untrusted Groovy script compiled through SandboxTransformer. The script controls the receiver/owner and method name used for a MethodClosure and controls invocation of that closure. Any script-reachable path that yields a plain groovy.lang.MethodClosure (e.g. the public constructor 'new MethodClosure(owner, "method")', or any runtime API returning one) is outside the transformer's rewrite of 'obj.&m'.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked whether Checker re-wraps or specially handles MethodClosure: it does not (grep of MethodClosure/invokeMethod shows references only in SandboxedMethodClosure and the transformer's MethodPointerExpression rewrite). Checked whether the transformer covers all method-pointer syntax: only MethodPointerExpression is rewritten, so only '&'-generated closures are protected. Checked whether InvokerChain blocks the call: InvokerChain only skips the chain for null receivers, irrelevant here; the default GroovyInterceptor passes the call through after notification. The unresolved point is acquisition of a plain MethodClosure without interceptor rejection (constructor call is itself intercepted as onNewInstance), so exploitability depends on host whitelist policy; this is not a runtime-confirmed escape.
candidates.impact: Sandbox policy bypass: a sandboxed script can invoke methods on objects for which the host interceptor would deny or restrict the call, because the interception layer records only a generic Closure 'call' on the MethodClosure wrapper. Depending on what the host exposes/denies, this can be the first step of a full sandbox escape/policy evasion (arbitrary method invocation on reachable objects).
candidates.prerequisites: SandboxTransformer is installed, and the application's interceptor chain (the library is deny-by-default only insofar as the host interceptor rejects calls) permits (a) acquiring a plain MethodClosure, i.e. does not reject the MethodClosure constructor/return value, and (b) invoking a Closure (Closure.call), which normal sandboxed scripts generally must be allowed to do. Requires Groovy 2.4.x MetaClassImpl special-casing of exact-class MethodClosure, which is the behavior documented in SandboxedMethodClosure's Javadoc but not verifiable from sources in this snapshot.
candidates.root_cause: SandboxTransformer only intercepts method pointers that appear as MethodPointerExpression, rewriting 'obj.&m' into new SandboxedMethodClosure(obj,'m') (SandboxTransformer.java:394-400). SandboxedMethodClosure is the only MethodClosure subclass whose doCall() routes through Checker.checkedCall (SandboxedMethodClosure.java:19-35); its Javadoc explicitly notes that Groovy's MetaClassImpl.invokeMethod special-cases objectClass == MethodClosure.class, so being a subclass is what forces normal doCall dispatch. Checker.checkedCall has special handling only for Class receivers (lines 86-101) and for Closure receivers/delegation (lines 103-137); it has no branch for MethodClosure and no re-wrapping of plain MethodClosure instances. Therefore a plain MethodClosure that reaches Checker falls into the generic VarArgInvokerChain path (lines 152-159): interceptors are shown only onMethodCall(receiver=<MethodClosure>, method='call'/'doCall', args), and the real owner.method(args) dispatch performed by MetaClassImpl for exact-class MethodClosure is never submitted to GroovyInterceptor.
candidates.title: Plain groovy.lang.MethodClosure invocations are not routed through Checker (method-pointer sandbox bypass)
candidates.trace: Script expression 'obj.&m' -> rewritten to SandboxedMethodClosure (checked path). Script obtaining a plain MethodClosure instead -> later call m(...) / m.call(...) -> Checker.checkedCall(m, false, false, 'call', args) -> Class branch skipped, Closure branch: pickMethod('call', ...) finds Closure.call so no delegation handling -> generic VarArgInvokerChain -> host interceptor sees only onMethodCall(receiver=m, method='call') -> default pass-through fakeCallSite('call').call(m,args) -> Groovy MetaClassImpl exact-MethodClosure special case -> owner.m(args) executed without onMethodCall(owner,'m',args) ever being reported to GroovyInterceptor.
candidates.unverified: Groovy 2.4.7's MetaClassImpl/MethodClosure dispatch is not present in the snapshot, so the exact special-case behavior is inferred from the SandboxedMethodClosure Javadoc, not read from Groovy source. No runtime test, no interceptor whitelist, and no end-to-end script path were executed; it is unverified whether a stock deny-by-default interceptor would allow obtaining a plain MethodClosure and whether any non-constructor runtime path yields one.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-863 Incorrect Authorization (sandbox/access-control bypass); also CWE-693 protection mechanism failure

coverage_summary: Reviewed all 27 model-visible files (22 Java files according to the relation index; the 5 remaining are pom.xml, README/index/site docs and test helpers). Main entry points read in full: SandboxTransformer (transformation of method calls, constructors incl. SECURITY-582 super-constructor handling, property/attribute/array access, casts, method pointers), Checker (all 620 lines), InvokerChain variants, ClosureSupport, SandboxedMethodClosure, Ops, Super, GroovyInterceptor, GroovyValueFilter, ScopeTracking transformer and StackVariableSet. The P1 relation index is partial and syntax-only (22 parsed Java files, 235 symbols, 508 edges, 561 unresolved calls, no control- or data-flow, no semantic resolution, no Spring/DI enforcement), so it was used only for navigation; every cited line was verified against source text. The snapshot contains no Groovy runtime/Groovy test sources (the .groovy test suite referenced by NonArrayConstructorList/TheTest is absent), so Groovy-internal dispatch behavior could not be inspected locally.
limitations: No Groovy 2.4.7 jar/source is part of the snapshot, so MetaClassImpl.invokeMethod's exact-class MethodClosure behavior and Closure call dispatch are inferred from source comments, not verified from dependency source.
The repository-visible test suite that would exercise the sandbox (SandboxTest/TheTest and robot tests) is not present in the model-visible snapshot; no regression or exploit test could be inspected.
No code was compiled or executed, and no interceptor whitelist implementation (the host application policy layer) is available, so attacker prerequisites and end-to-end impact remain unverified.
The relation index reports partial coverage (11 omitted files, unresolved calls) and supports only syntax/navigation candidates, not reachability or data flow.
Only files inside the assigned source root were reviewed; dependency behavior of Groovy 2.4.7 and of the JVM reflection/meta-class machinery was not reviewed.

rejected_leads.lead: Compiler-generated calls for switch/case ('isCase') and for-in ('iterator') are not rewritten by SandboxTransformer.innerTransform
rejected_leads.reason: No SwitchStatement/case-dispatch handling exists in the transformer, but the claim that these calls are emitted outside the AST is based on Groovy compiler knowledge not present in the snapshot, and no concrete dangerous isCase/iterator implementation (or interception-independent exploit chain) could be established, so it did not reach the evidence threshold.

rejected_leads.lead: checkedCast interface probing / positional-constructor casts could be bypassed
rejected_leads.reason: Checker.checkedCast (Checker.java:539-606) deliberately enumerates interface methods and positional-constructor arguments and submits them to the interceptor chain before delegating to ScriptBytecodeAdapter.asType/castToType; the exclusion for java.util collection targets is narrow and no unguarded escape path was found in source.

rejected_leads.lead: InvokerChain disables interception when receiver is null
rejected_leads.reason: InvokerChain (lines 15-24) builds an empty interceptor chain for null receivers, but a null receiver cannot dispatch an instance operation, and checkedGetProperty/checkedComparison's null short-circuits (Checker.java:247, 515-518) only fall back to null-safe static helpers; no attacker-controlled dispatch was identified.

rejected_leads.lead: Closure delegation special-casing (ClosureSupport.targetsOf, isInvokingMethodOnClosure, BUILTIN_PROPERTIES) may still miss dispatch paths
rejected_leads.reason: The code explicitly chases owner/delegate targets through checkedCall and maps closure.invokeMethod/getProperty/setProperty to the real target; no concrete unhandled case could be demonstrated from this snapshot, so it remains an unconfirmed lead.

summary: Repository is the groovy-sandbox library (pom version 1.20-SNAPSHOT, Groovy 2.4.7 dependency), a compile-time Groovy AST transformer plus a runtime Checker that forwards intercepted calls to per-thread GroovyInterceptor chains. I read all 27 model-visible files: the transformer (SandboxTransformer, ScopeTracking…, StackVariableSet), the runtime checking layer (Checker, InvokerChain variants, ClosureSupport, SandboxedMethodClosure, Ops, Super) and the 7 test helper classes. The most plausible security-relevant gap is that sandbox protection for the Groovy method-pointer operator exists only for MethodPointerExpression rewritten at compile time to SandboxedMethodClosure; at runtime there is no equivalent guard for any other groovy.lang.MethodClosure. Because Groovy's MetaClassImpl special-cases receivers whose exact class is MethodClosure (the condition the SandboxedMethodClosure Javadoc was written about), invoking a plain MethodClosure executes the owner.method(...) dispatch without Checker/GroovyInterceptor seeing the owner and method, leaving the sandbox policy applied only to the wrapper call. I could not verify a fully interceptor-independent acquisition path for a plain MethodClosure from the snapshot alone, so this is submitted as a lead with explicit counterevidence, not a confirmed vulnerability.
